name: parted
description: A partition editor that works both interactively and in scripts, with GPT support and online resizing.

flags.description: Create a new GPT label (DESTROYS the existing table).
Create a partition, e.g. mkpart primary ext4 1MiB 100%.
Resize partition N to a new end position (online-capable).

examples.output:
Model: ATA Samsung SSD 860
Disk /dev/sdb: 500GB
Partition Table: gpt
Number  Start  End    Size   File system  Name
 1      1049kB 500GB  500GB  ext4         data
examples.explanation: Shows the disk model, table type (gpt), and partitions with exact byte positions.

examples.command: sudo parted -s /dev/sdb mklabel gpt mkpart data ext4 1MiB 100%
examples.explanation: Scripted setup: new GPT label plus one ext4-typed partition spanning the disk. The -s flag prevents prompts.
Grows partition 2 to fill the disk — typically followed by growpart, then resize2fs (ext4) or xfs_growfs (xfs) on the filesystem.

about: parted positions are exact: units like MiB/GiB avoid rounding surprises (use 1MiB, not 0%, for alignment). Unlike fdisk it applies commands immediately — there is no w confirmation step. resizepart works on mounted partitions when the kernel supports it, making it the tool for growing cloud volumes.
mistakes: Forgetting that parted applies changes instantly — no undo.
Using 0% as start and getting misaligned partitions on some disks.
warnings: mklabel destroys the partition table immediately. On the wrong disk, that is instant data loss.
